version: v2 (hand-verified 2026-11-24 against upstream dolevf/Damn-Vulnerable-GraphQL-Application tag 2.2.0, commit a961308c02d1fb462b192681c336b0739e432da7, version.py VERSION='2.2.0'; use image dolevf/dvga:2.2.0; every entry's 'source' cites the resolver, helper, middleware or template that carries it; entries are deliberately coarse: component + class + mechanism, no line numbers)
task_goal_template: Map and hunt the highest-signal security weaknesses of the deliberately vulnerable GraphQL training application at {url}: GraphQL information disclosure, injection (SQL, OS command, stored XSS), server-side request forgery, authorization bypass and arbitrary file write. Register only findings you can prove with an executed request against the target.
notes: DVGA listens on container port 5013 by default (config.WEB_PORT, http://localhost:5013); the host port can be remapped with WEB_PORT, and the app binds to 127.0.0.1 by default (config.WEB_HOST).

Difficulty is server-wide persistent state (ServerMode.hardened in the SQLite DB, default False = Beginner), not per request: GET /difficulty/<easy|hard> or any request carrying the header X-DVGA-MODE (Expert -> hard, anything else -> easy; views.set_difficulty before_request hook) flips it for every client. This ground truth assumes Beginner mode. In Expert mode the depth/cost/introspection/deny-list/operation-name middlewares activate, strip_dangerous_characters removes ';' and '&', allowed_cmds restricts systemDiagnostics, and /graphiql is disabled outright.

Expert-mode-only protections and their bypasses (not graded here, because they are inactive in Beginner mode): security.on_denylist blocks only the whitespace-normalised exact strings '{systemHealth}' and 'query{systemHealth}' (an operation name or alias gets through); security.operation_name_allowed accepts any query that uses an allowed operation name such as getPastes; IntrospectionMiddleware blocks only the __schema field (__type is not blocked). A scanner finding on these is a discovery candidate.
All denial-of-service scenarios (batch query, deep recursion, aliases, field duplication, resource-intensive systemUpdate) are deliberately excluded so the noise governor is not rewarded for DoS.

Checked and omitted: log injection / HTML injection on /audit. templates/audit.html renders gqloperation and gqlquery through Jinja autoescape with no |safe, so no HTML injection was found there in 2.2.0; spoofed operation names in the audit log are an integrity weakness rather than an injection.
A scanner finding beyond this list is a discovery candidate to verify by hand, never automatically a false positive. Treat a corpus upgrade as a ground-truth version bump, not a silent edit.

findings.title: GraphQL introspection enabled
findings.proof_hint: POSTing an introspection query (__schema { types { name fields { name } } }) to /graphql returns the full schema including importPaste, systemDebug, systemDiagnostics and uploadPaste
findings.source: core/middleware.py IntrospectionMiddleware.resolve returns next() immediately when helpers.is_level_easy(); otherwise it rejects only the __schema field. core/views.py registers it in gql_middlew on the /graphql view.

findings.title: GraphiQL interactive IDE exposed
findings.proof_hint: GET /graphiql (Accept: text/html) serves the GraphiQL IDE page to an unauthenticated session; executing a query from it additionally needs the cookie bypass in GT-011
findings.source: core/views.py app.add_url_rule('/graphiql', OverriddenView.as_view(..., graphiql=True, middleware=igql_middlew)); core/view_override.py OverriddenView.dispatch_request renders GraphiQL on GET. The only guard is the resolver middleware IGQLProtectionMiddleware, which does not run for the page itself.

findings.title: GraphQL field suggestions leak schema names
findings.proof_hint: a query with a misspelled field (e.g. { pastse { id } }) returns 'Cannot query field "pastse" on type "Query". Did you mean "pastes" or "paste"?', enabling schema recovery even if introspection is blocked
findings.source: graphql-core 2.3.2 (pinned in requirements.txt) graphql/validation/rules/fields_on_correct_type.py _undefined_field_message appends 'Did you mean ...?'. DVGA does not disable suggestions; the /graphql view uses default error formatting, which passes the message through.

findings.title: SSRF through the importPaste mutation
findings.proof_hint: importPaste(host:"127.0.0.1", port:5013, path:"/", scheme:"http") makes the server fetch that URL with curl and return the response body in result (and store it as a private paste)
findings.source: core/views.py ImportPaste.mutate builds url = f"{scheme}://{host}:{port}{path}" and runs helpers.run_cmd(f'curl --insecure {url}'), returning the output as result and as the content of a new private Paste. No host allow-list.

findings.title: OS command injection in importPaste
findings.proof_hint: shell metacharacters in the host, path or scheme argument (e.g. path:"/; id") make the server run the injected command; its output appears in result and in the imported paste
findings.source: core/views.py ImportPaste.mutate passes the interpolated URL through security.strip_dangerous_characters (a no-op in Beginner mode; strips only ';' and '&' in Expert mode, leaving '|', '$()' and backticks) into helpers.run_cmd, which is os.popen(cmd).read() (core/helpers.py), so the string is run by a shell. port is a GraphQL Int and is not injectable.

findings.title: OS command injection in systemDebug (and command execution in systemDiagnostics)
findings.proof_hint: systemDebug(arg:"; id") returns the output of the injected command after the ps listing; systemDiagnostics(username:"admin", password:<admin password>, cmd:"id") runs cmd directly
findings.source: core/views.py Query.resolve_system_debug runs helpers.run_cmd('ps {}'.format(arg)) unauthenticated with no filtering. Query.resolve_system_diagnostics runs helpers.run_cmd(cmd) once security.check_creds matches the admin user's real password; security.allowed_cmds returns True for any cmd in Beginner mode. The admin password is recoverable through GT-007 or GT-009.

findings.title: SQL injection in the pastes query filter argument
findings.proof_hint: a tautology or UNION payload in pastes(filter:"...") changes the result set (e.g. filter:"x' or 1=1 --" returns pastes beyond the filter, or a UNION reads the users table)
findings.source: core/views.py Query.resolve_pastes applies result.filter(text("title = '%s' or content = '%s'" % (filter, filter))), interpolating the argument into raw SQL via sqlalchemy.text.

findings.title: Stored XSS through createPaste content/title
findings.proof_hint: a paste created with an HTML payload in title or content (e.g. ) renders as markup and executes when /public_pastes (or /my_pastes for private pastes) is viewed
findings.source:
core/views.py CreatePaste.mutate and EditPaste.mutate store title/content verbatim. templates/paste.html builds paste cards with template literals (${title}, 
${content}
) and inserts them with jQuery .append() into #public_gallery / #private_gallery, and the same for pastes arriving over the paste subscription, with no escaping.

findings.title: JWT signature not verified: forged token impersonates admin
findings.proof_hint: me(token:<any JWT whose payload is {"identity":"admin"}, signature arbitrary or alg none, expiry ignored>) { username password } returns the admin user with the real password instead of '******'
findings.source: core/helpers.py get_identity decodes with jwt.decode(token, options={'verify_signature': False, 'verify_exp': False}) and returns the 'identity' claim. core/views.py Query.resolve_me writes that identity into info.context.json['identity'] and looks the user up by it; UserObject.resolve_password returns the real password when info.context.json.get('identity') == 'admin'. (app.py also hard-codes JWT_SECRET_KEY='dvga', so tokens can be signed validly too.)

findings.title: Arbitrary file write / path traversal in uploadPaste filename
findings.proof_hint: uploadPaste with a filename containing ../ sequences writes the supplied content outside pastes/; a filename into a missing directory (e.g. ../nope/x.txt) returns the OS error naming the unsanitised path 'pastes/../nope/x.txt', which proves the concatenation without writing anything
findings.source: core/views.py UploadPaste.mutate calls helpers.save_file(filename, content). core/helpers.py save_file does open(WEB_UPLOADDIR + filename, 'w') with WEB_UPLOADDIR = 'pastes/' (config.py) and no normalisation or containment check, and returns str(exception) as the result on failure.

findings.title: GraphiQL access control bypass via client-controlled cookie
findings.proof_hint: a query POSTed to /graphiql is rejected with 'GraphiQL Access Rejected' when the env cookie is absent or graphiql:disable, and executes once the request carries Cookie: env=graphiql:enable
findings.source: core/middleware.py IGQLProtectionMiddleware.resolve allows execution only when request.cookies.get('env') == 'graphiql:enable' (and always rejects in Expert mode); core/views.py index() sets env=graphiql:disable on the client, so the gate is a value the client controls.

findings.title: Stack traces disclosed in GraphiQL endpoint errors
findings.proof_hint: an invalid query (e.g. a misspelled field) POSTed to /graphiql returns errors[].extensions.exception with stack, debug and path entries exposing Python source paths
findings.source: core/views.py registers /graphiql with format_error=format_custom_error; core/view_override.py format_custom_error adds extensions.exception.stack (traceback.format_stack), .debug (traceback.format_exc) and .path to every error except 'GraphiQL Access Rejected'. /graphql uses the default formatter and does not leak traces.
